- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model tends to overestimate prices after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 70+ values), often overshooting by 2–5%.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not fully captured.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 7–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits high variance in short-term predictions (especially days 1–5), suggesting it overreacts to recent volatility.
- Model fails to capture the “rebound” effect after price drops — often underestimates recovery in the 10–15 day window.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp reversals or sudden spikes in the true outcome.
- Model’s forecast mean is typically 1–3% below the true outcome mean over the 30-day horizon, indicating a consistent downward bias.
- Model overcorrects after recent high prices, leading to artificial “pullback” forecasts that don’t align with actual market behavior.
